card.name: Sogdian Whirl dance
card.era: first half 1st millennium CE; peak Tang dynasty
card.tagline: Spinning Silk Road dance of whirling Sogdian performers
card.profile: The Sogdian Whirl (胡旋, Húxuán) was a Central Asian dance imported into China in the first half of the first millennium CE, in which a dancer spun rapidly within a small circle on a round carpet (English Wikipedia). Especially popular in Tang Chang'an and Luoyang, it was performed at court — reputedly by Yang Guifei and An Lushan — and is depicted in Sogdian and Chinese funerary art and Dunhuang murals (Smithsonian; CGTN).
card.insight: Celebrated in Bai Juyi's poem 'The Whirling Girl,' the dance symbolizes the cosmopolitan, outward-looking spirit of the Tang dynasty and Silk Road cultural exchange (Smithsonian 'The Sogdians'; China Daily).
